methodological_rigor.justification: This is a preclinical study combining in vitro evaluation (pH sensitivity, cytotoxicity, uptake mechanism in K1 and 8505C thyroid cancer cell lines) with orthotopic nude mouse models for in vivo labeling and fluorescence-guided surgery (Abstract). The design is appropriate for proof-of-concept margin visualization, and the work includes histologic confirmation of complete resection and margin status (Abstract; Results 3.5). Key limitations are inherent to the model system (cell line xenografts rather than patient-derived tumors, and uncertain generalizability to indolent thyroid cancers) and are acknowledged (Discussion, Limitations). Statistical reporting includes quantified tumor-to-background ratios and hypothesis testing (e.g., TBR difference with p = 0.003 in the K1 model) (Results 3.4), but broader details on randomization/blinding and power are not prominent in the blinded text.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is preclinical (cell line and orthotopic mouse models) and therefore maps to Oxford LoE 5 per the rubric (Abstract). Clinically, intraoperative margin assessment is a real unmet need in thyroid surgery, and the study demonstrates rapid, topical, tumor-specific fluorescence with histology-correlated detection of macroscopic and microscopic positive margins in vivo (Abstract; Discussion). The translational relevance is plausible but remains unproven without human tissue or clinical feasibility data.

reporting_quality.justification: Given the animal-model centerpiece (orthotopic nude mouse models with fluorescence-guided surgery), ARRIVE is the most applicable reporting standard (Methods/Results). The manuscript reports model types (K1 and 8505C), some sample sizes (e.g., 8505C model n = 10), quantified TBRs over sequential washes, and histopathologic validation of resection completeness (Abstract; Results 3.4–3.6). However, key ARRIVE elements such as explicit randomization/blinding statements, priori sample-size justification, and full protocol transparency are not clearly detailed in the blinded text. Data/code availability is not specified beyond the methods narrative.

novelty_literature.justification: The concept of fluorescence-guided surgery is established, but a sprayable, pH-sensitive near-infrared probe tailored for rapid topical labeling and margin assessment in thyroid cancer is a relatively novel formulation and use case (Abstract/Introduction). The manuscript adds novelty by demonstrating repeated-wash robustness and correspondence of fluorescence patterns with histologic margins, including microscopic PSM detection in orthotopic models (Abstract; Results). This is a strong preclinical technical advance, though not yet clinically validated.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is comprehensive, clearly separating in vitro characterization, in vivo orthotopic model testing, and the fluorescence-guided surgery workflow with histologic validation. Results are structured by experimental stage (wash quantification, FGS, histology, second model validation) and provide concrete quantitative summaries (e.g., TBR values across washes; p-values) (Results 3.4–3.6). The discussion appropriately situates the approach and states limitations and next steps (Discussion).

key_strengths: End-to-end preclinical demonstration: in vitro probe characterization, orthotopic mouse model labeling, fluorescence-guided surgery, and histologic confirmation of margins (Abstract; Results 3.4–3.6).
Quantified tumor-to-background ratios that remain distinguishable after multiple washes, supporting robustness of topical application (Results 3.6).
Acknowledges model limitations and proposes higher-fidelity follow-up (e.g., PDOX models) to support translation (Discussion, Limitations).
key_concerns: Evidence is limited to cell line xenografts; human-tissue testing and broader model diversity are needed to support clinical translation claims (Discussion, Limitations).
Animal-study rigor elements (randomization, blinding, sample-size justification) are not clearly reported in the blinded text, limiting confidence in bias control (Methods/Results).
Data/code/protocol sharing is not described, constraining reproducibility beyond the narrative methods.
chief_reviewer.rationale: A compelling preclinical technical advance with clear histology-backed proof-of-concept, but Tier 2 acceptance would require major revisions that strengthen animal-study rigor reporting and provide additional validation steps toward translation.
